Quick jump

Ordered vs Sold by category core retail only

Sell-through = period units sold ÷ period units ordered (from your invoices). Over 100% = selling faster than these suppliers delivered, or another distributor also supplies that category (e.g. milk, water, juice, most iced-coffee). Under ~50% = ordering ahead of sales / building stock. Net stock = opening stock + units ordered − units sold (POS stock-on-hand figures are ignored — not reconciled with receiving; opening stock is the 26 Nov 2025 handover stocktake); "+N pend." = that many ordered lines aren't matched to a sale yet, and lines sold but not yet matched to any supplier's invoices are excluded until you load that supplier.

Monthly order spend by category (incl GST)

POS sales are a single whole-period figure, so only the ordering side has a monthly trend here.

Category summary

What you ordered — every product (all suppliers)

What you sold — POS PLU report

Net stock = opening stock + units ordered − units sold, computed here — the POS report's own stock-on-hand figures are not used (that stock file isn't kept in sync with deliveries). Opening stock comes from the 26 Nov 2025 handover stocktake. "pending" = no order match yet, so ordered qty is unknown. GP% and revenue are ex-GST.

Profit — what's changed

    Real margin = what the till sold each item for (ex GST) minus what your supplier invoices say that unit actually cost, on the day it sold. The till's own cost prices come from the franchise price file and run high, so its GP% understates your real margin. Fuel, card surcharges, caravan park fees and gift-card sales are left out — shop trade only.

    Daily profit margin

    Real GP% uses invoice costs; Till GP% is what the POS reports; after PF overheads also takes off Pie Face delivery charges + packaging (cups, bags, lids), which never show against a product. Invoice-costed = share of the day's sales with a real invoice cost behind it — the rest (tobacco, milk/iced coffee and other suppliers whose invoices aren't loaded) use the till's cost. One new row lands every night with the PLU sales email.

    Supplier cost changes last 30 days of invoices, ±5% or more

    Latest invoice unit cost vs the purchase before it. A jump is often a special ending rather than a real price rise — either way it comes straight off margin, since sell prices are fixed. Weekly impact = change × current weekly sales (blank when weekly sales aren't tracked for that line).

    Monthly trend

    POS category totals (as exported)

    Straight from the SwiftPOS report's group totals. Some groups are only exported as a total (no per-product lines), so the "What you sold" tab doesn't cover everything — re-run the PLU Sales report with all groups expanded / show detail for full SKU coverage. POS group names in this store are often mis-assigned, so a few lines land in the wrong category here.

    Other supplier spend — overview only not linked to sales

    These 20 suppliers are operating costs, not resale stock (fuel cards, insurance, gas bottle swap aside, waste, freight, plumbing, ice, coffee, ink/toner, etc.) — there's no "sold units" to match them against. Totals are extracted per-document (invoice or statement) and are a rough overview, not a reconciled ledger: a supplier that emails both an invoice and a later statement for the same charge will be counted twice here, and figures marked est. come from the largest dollar figure found in a document that had no clearly labelled total — treat those as approximate.

    Wastage — not loaded yet

    Send a wastage / stock-adjustment / spoilage report and it slots in here as a 4th column (Ordered → Sold → Stock → Wasted) on every product, plus a wastage $ by category chart and a "shrink rate" (wasted ÷ ordered) flag.

    Easiest formats: CSV or Excel with columns date, product / PLU / barcode, qty, and (if you have it) reason and cost. PDF is fine too.

    How this is built & what to trust

    • Orders come from your actual invoices: TCW, Coke (CCEP), Pie Face (Superior Food Group), Asahi, Unilever (Streets), Elgas (gas bottle swap only), More Ice (bagged ice), D Jays Gourmet (Truckin' Jerky / Biltong) and Pacific Optics (Aerial-branded sunglasses, reading glasses, headwear, footwear, phone accessories, batteries, toys), Dec 2025 – Aug 2026. Quantities are what was shipped / billed. Pacific Optics invoices and credit notes are often emailed twice in two different layouts (an Opmetrix CRM confirmation and a formal accounting copy) - these are matched by transaction ID and only counted once.
    • Sales (units, revenue, GP) come from a database of SwiftPOS "PLU Sales" exports — monthly at first, then one short export a day emailed in automatically — covering 26 Nov 2025 to the most recent import. Overlapping exports are detected and only counted once (the wider one wins), so re-sent or re-ranged exports can't double up a day's sales.
    • Other supplier spend (see that tab) covers ~17 more suppliers — insurance, fuel cards, waste, freight, plumbing, coffee, ink/toner and similar operating costs. These aren't resale stock, so there's no sell-through for them: it's a rough $-by-month overview, not reconciled against sales, and can double-count a supplier that emails both an invoice and a later statement for the same charge.
    • Stock is calculated, not taken from the POS. The POS stock-on-hand figures are unreliable (the stock file isn't reconciled with receiving), so Net stock = opening stock + units ordered − units sold over the window. Opening stock comes from the 27-page Orison Stocktaking report taken on 26 Nov 2025, the day the business changed hands — its 708 counted lines are matched to POS products by exact description (verbatim-identical naming in ~two-thirds of cases; the rest are slow-moving lines, mostly automotive, with no matching PLU sold in the tracked period). It still assumes no wastage — treat it as net movement, not a shelf count. A product with no order match shows pending until its supplier's invoices are loaded.
    • Order ↔ sale linking is automatic fuzzy name matching (no shared barcode between the invoice and the till). Each linked row shows a confidence 0–1. Only matches ≥ 0.55 are treated as linked. To lock or fix a match, edit product_map.csv (next to this file): put the correct POS PLU in the LOCKED_plu column and re-run the build.
    • Pooled estimate rows (Red Bull, Monster, V) are a deliberate exception to 1:1 linking: these brands' 4-packs are routinely broken open and sold as loose singles under whichever flavour's till button a staff member presses, so there's no record of which flavour a dismantled can became. Rather than guess a specific (likely wrong) flavour match, any order or POS line left over after normal matching is pooled with the rest of its brand + can size + sugar-free-or-not, and the pooled sales are split back across the pooled orders by their own volume share. Treat the sell-through on these as a good estimate for that whole group, not a per-flavour fact.
    • Categories are derived from the product name, not the POS group (this store's POS groups are inconsistent). Drinks are split Energy / Sports / Soft / Water / Juice / Iced Coffee & Milk / Iced Tea. Ice Cream (Magnum, Gaytime, Paddle Pop, Cornetto, …), Gas Bottles (Elgas Swap'n'Go 8.5kg / 3.7kg vs the POS "BBQ Gas" PLUs), Bagged Ice (More Ice 5kg vs the POS "5KG ICE BAG" PLUs), and Pacific Optics' Sunglasses & Eyewear, Headwear, Footwear, Phone Accessories, Batteries and Toys & Novelty are all their own categories, pulled out of whatever POS group they'd otherwise land in — several of those POS groups (BBQ Gas, Ice, Sunglasses, Headwear, Thongs, Batteries, Readers, Toys) used to be treated as non-retail junk entirely.
    • Coverage gaps: the POS export has ~1,700 product lines plus ~116 collapsed group totals. Categories like milk, water, juice and iced coffee sell far more than TCW+Coke supply — those come from other distributors not yet loaded, so their net stock shows pending. Add them one invoice set at a time and this page grows.

    System notes for a future Claude session, not the owner

    This tab is a runbook, not a dashboard feature — written so a Claude session with no memory of building this can orient itself and troubleshoot without the owner having to re-explain the whole system. If you're Claude and something's wrong, read this tab first, then the relevant script (they're short and commented for exactly this reason).

    Folder layout

    • Invoices\ (this file's folder) — one subfolder per supplier (TCW, Coke\Sorted Invoices, Superior = Pie Face, Asahi, Unilever, Elgas, More Ice, D Jays Gourmet, Pacific Optics, plus ~20 operating-expense supplier folders), PLU Sales\ (daily/monthly SwiftPOS exports), _opening_stock\ (the 26 Nov 2025 handover stocktake PDF), _Inbox_Review\ (unrecognized-sender staging), product_map.csv (manual match overrides).
    • Invoices\_dashboard_tools\ — every script in this pipeline, plus dashboard_data.json (the data this HTML is rendered from) and tenterfield.db (SQLite, POS sales + opening stock).
    • C:\Users\neell\.invoice-sync\ — deliberately outside OneDrive so the Gmail app password in config.json never syncs to the cloud. Holds check_inbox.py (nightly job), full_scan.py (one-off historical re-scan), supplier_map.py (sender routing rules, shared by both), and logs\YYYY-MM-DD.log / last_run.txt.

    Nightly automation

    • The nightly run is the GitHub Actions job only (.github/workflows/nightly-sync.yml → _dashboard_tools/cloud_check_inbox.py, ~23:25 local, commits straight to main); "Last night's automation" reads its cloud_sync_status.json. The old laptop Task Scheduler task UnitedTenterfieldInboxSync (running check_inbox.py) was disabled 3 Oct 2026 at the owner's request — it checked the same inbox with its own separate "already processed" list, so both pipelines imported the same emails and the laptop copy drifted from GitHub. Not deleted: Enable-ScheduledTask -TaskName UnitedTenterfieldInboxSync restores it, but only if the owner asks. Always git pull before working on the laptop copy. The check_inbox.py description below still applies to cloud_check_inbox.py, which uses the same logic.
    • check_inbox.py searches the inbox for the last lookback_days (3) days. For each message: a self-sent PDF/Excel is tested as a PLU Sales export (try_import_plu_attachment) — imported only if its date span is ≤3 days (a wider span is logged and skipped, never auto-trusted: this guards against a repeat of the Sep-2025-dated export incident that once nearly corrupted the sales history). Anything else is routed by supplier_map.resolve_known_folder(): TCW gets date/total extracted from the PDF and is renamed TCW DDMonYY total [INVxxxx].PDF; every other known supplier is filed as-is (content-hash deduped against the whole tree); EXCLUDE_SENDERS are silently dropped; anything unrecognized lands in _Inbox_Review. If anything was filed, rebuild.py runs automatically at the end.
    • Coke is the one exception: no email address has ever delivered a real Coke tax invoice here (only collections notices from aus.coke.credit@ccamatil.com) — those still have to be saved by hand into Coke\Sorted Invoices\ (any filename; parse_coke.py reads it by content, not name) and the dashboard rebuilt.
    • To add a newly-recognized supplier or fix a misrouted sender, edit the tables in supplier_map.py (SENDER_FOLDER / DOMAIN_FOLDER / SHARED_RELAY_DOMAINS+RELAY_NAME_ALIASES for shared platforms like MYOB where the address alone doesn't identify the sender / EXCLUDE_SENDERS) — both check_inbox.py and full_scan.py read the same file, so it never drifts between the nightly job and a manual historical re-scan.

    Rebuild pipeline

    Run python rebuild.py from _dashboard_tools\ any time by hand; it's the same thing the nightly job triggers automatically.

    • parse.py / parse_coke.py / parse_pf.py / parse_asahi.py / parse_unilever.py / parse_elgas.py / parse_moreice.py / parse_djays.py / parse_pacificoptics.py — one per product supplier, each reads that supplier's own folder and writes a *_orders.json (or invoices.json for TCW). Every one of these reads individual per-invoice PDFs directly from disk — content-based extraction, no filename conventions relied on, no merged/combined-PDF step anywhere (Coke used to work that way; it doesn't any more, on purpose, to match everyone else).
    • parse_expense.py — rough $-by-month overview for ~20 operating-expense suppliers (insurance, fuel cards, waste, etc.) that don't get full product-level integration.
    • sync_plu.py — calls import_plu.py --scan, which imports any not-yet-seen file in PLU Sales\ into tenterfield.db via db.py. Each import keeps its own [period_start, period_end]; a wider later import automatically supersedes a narrower one it fully contains, so overlapping exports never double-count (see db.recompute_supersession).
    • build_data.py — the actual join. Loads all the orders + db.get_combined_sales(), fuzzy-matches order lines to POS PLUs via match.py (norm_tokens / canon_size / score — Jaccard + brand-token bonus + size bonus, ≥0.55 counts as linked), applies product_map.csv's LOCKED_plu overrides (round-tripped: it reads the old file's locks before overwriting it, so a manual fix survives every future rebuild), pools generic no-flavour Red Bull/Monster/V multipack lines (POOL_BRANDS) since dismantled 4-packs can't be honestly assigned to one flavour, folds in opening stock from import_stocktake.py's 26 Nov 2025 baseline, and calls sync_status.py (automation status) and scan_alerts.py (bill/notice keyword scan, 60-day window, one per supplier, corroboration required for generic words like "overdue" to avoid flagging routine statement column headers). Writes dashboard_data.json. (There used to be an on-page Inbox Review panel here too - removed 18 Sep 2026, the owner has other plans for that surface. The underlying mechanism is unaffected: unrecognized senders still land in _Inbox_Review, untouched, via check_inbox.py - only the dashboard UI for triaging it is gone.)
    • profit.py — the Profit tab (called from build_data.py). Re-costs every daily PLU line from supplier invoices (mean of the last ≤3 purchases on/before that day, via the order↔PLU links plus a ≥0.8 name match for pooled/unlinked PLUs, with a pack-size factor checked against the till's cost) because the till's franchise cost prices run 3–6% high (Asahi ~27%). No invoice → falls back to the till's cost (shown as "Invoice-costed" coverage); no cost at all → left out. BREAK_PACKS lists lines bought as multipacks and sold singly (Drink Up 1.5L = 6-pack ÷ 6) — add to it if the owner starts breaking up another pack. Excludes fuel, surcharges, caravan park and gift-card lines. Pie Face delivery + packaging is applied as a separate "after PF overheads" figure.
    • build_html.py — renders dashboard_data.json into this file, a single self-contained HTML page with the data embedded as JSON. This file (build_html.py) is also where the "Ask Claude" widget, the automation/alerts/inbox-review panels, and this very tab live — if the owner asks for a dashboard UI change, it's the one to edit.

    This page's two lives

    The exact same build_html.py output is used two ways, and the difference matters when troubleshooting:

    • Local file — Invoices\United Tenterfield Dashboard.html, rewritten by every rebuild, opened by the owner via file://. No window.claude here, so the "Ask Claude" button and CSV-export-via-downloads-capability both silently no-op to their plain fallback (a real <a download> for CSV). This is the one that's always current.
    • Hosted artifact — a copy published to claude.ai with capabilities: {sample:{}, downloads:true} declared, so the chat and CSV export work for real there. It is a frozen snapshot from whenever it was last published — the nightly automation only ever touches the local file, and nothing on this laptop can push to a hosted artifact (that requires the Artifact tool inside a live Claude Code session). Its supplier-folder / bill-alert file links are also dead there: the actual PDFs were never uploaded to it. If the owner says the hosted link looks stale or its links don't open anything, that's expected, not a bug — it needs a fresh Artifact publish of the current local file, same URL, from a live session.

    Known quirks worth knowing before you "fix" them

    • Windows' filesystem is case-insensitive: glob("*.pdf") already matches .PDF, so a second glob for the uppercase pattern double-counts every file. Bit us once in parse_coke.py; grep for a second glob call before adding one anywhere.
    • twdadmin@tcwtwd.com.au routes to a TWD folder that is deliberately never parsed — it's a different business's account on the same wholesaler, not this store's stock.
    • Bill-alert scanning treats "OVERDUE"/"PAST DUE" as weak signals (need a nearby phrase like "please pay") because they're routine column headers on almost every AR statement; only stronger phrases (STOP SUPPLY, FINAL NOTICE, etc.) count on their own. If a real overdue notice isn't showing up, it's probably worded in a way neither keyword list catches — check scan_alerts.py's STRONG_KEYWORDS/WEAK_KEYWORDS.
    • "Net stock" is a computed movement (opening stock + ordered − sold), never read from the POS's own stock-on-hand field, which isn't kept in sync with receiving. A product showing "pending" simply has no confident order↔sale link yet, not zero stock.

    If something looks wrong, in order

    1. Check this dashboard's "Last night's automation" and "Bills & account notices" panels first — they already surface the most common failure modes.
    2. C:\Users\neell\.invoice-sync\logs\ — the actual night's log, one block per run.
    3. Re-run python rebuild.py by hand from _dashboard_tools\ and read its console output; each step prints its own row/total counts, so a step that silently produced zero rows is easy to spot.
    4. python db.py (from _dashboard_tools\) prints every PLU-sales import and whether it's active or superseded — useful if sales figures look off.
    5. Ask the owner what changed recently before assuming the code is wrong — most issues so far have been a new sender, a new export format, or a genuinely new/renamed product, not a bug.
